candidate.title: Cross-instance credential sync incorrectly trusts req.body.userId, attaching credentials to the wrong local user
candidate.file: UNKNOWN (not in PR diff) — locate the sync handler that reads req.body.userId and queries the local User table
reports: [advisory] the handler resolves reqbody.userid — the calling instance's user id — directly against the local user table with no cross-instance identity mapping or scoping beyond the shared secret. on any deployment whose local user ids do not mirror the parent's id space, synced credentials are attached to an unrelated local user, so that user's bookings and meetings silently route through a stranger's calendar/video account.

[bug] the handler trusts the parent's raw numeric userid to identify the local user (the schema comment says 'userid of the cal.com user') with no cross-instance identity mapping or verification such as an email check. unless the child instance's user id space is kept identical to cal.com's, the webhook delivers one cal.com user's oauth credentials to the local user holding the same numeric id — a different person — who then books meetings through another user's calendar; any user created or deleted on either side diverges the id spaces and nothing in the design detects it.
